subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and which canonical fields and trust semantics should flow through Gateway protocol, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: Current main has multiple partial attribution mechanisms, but choosing the permanent sender identity shape affects public APIs, session state, UI rendering, and security/trust boundaries.

options.title: Design additive sender identity contract
options.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate `senderLabel`, provenance, and UI rendering to consume it while preserving existing compatible behavior.

options.title: Continue narrow attribution fixes
options.body: Keep fixing specific regressions such as sessions_send requester names and WebChat senderLabel fallbacks without committing to a broad identity contract yet.

options.title: Defer to broader multi-agent model
options.body: Keep this as canonical design work until broader multi-agent conversation and permission semantics are ready to own sender identity end to end.

recommendation.title: Design additive sender identity contract
recommendation.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate `senderLabel`, provenance, and UI rendering to consume it while preserving existing compatible behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans provenance/session contracts and multi-agent UX direction, and steipete has relevant provenance/session history plus prior discussion on this item.
